methods.label: Square the pension relationships and eliminate
methods.explanation:
Use the contextual conditions \(a,b,p,q>0\), with the data compatible with the stated pension rule. Let \(t\geq0\) be the original years of service, let \(P\) be the original annual pension, and let \(k>0\) be the proportionality constant. Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
P&=k\sqrt t,\\
P+p&=k\sqrt{t+a},\\
P+q&=k\sqrt{t+b}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Squaring is useful because it turns the extra years of service into simple differences. All the pension amounts are nonnegative, so there is no sign ambiguity. Subtracting \(P^2=k^2t\) from the other two squared equations gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
2Pp+p^2&=ak^2,\\
2Pq+q^2&=bk^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Multiply the first equation by \(b\) and the second by \(a\), then subtract to eliminate \(k^2\):
\[
2P(bp-aq)=aq^2-bp^2.
\]
Before dividing, we must check that \(bp-aq\neq0\). If \(bp=aq\), this last equation also gives \(aq^2=bp^2\). Substituting \(bp=aq\) yields \(aq(q-p)=0\). Positivity forces \(q=p\), and then \(bp=aq\) forces \(b=a\), contrary to the hypothesis.

Therefore the annual pension is
\[
\boxed{P=\frac{aq^2-bp^2}{2(bp-aq)}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
